title: Iso-Cost Fidelity Map and Knee-Finder for Mixed-Precision Decisions
content:
Purpose
This note documents a conceptual calculator and an associated spreadsheet layout for producing iso-cost vs fidelity contour maps across INT8, FP8, and 4-bit (4b) quantization options. The goal is to provide a pragmatic, testable decision surface teams can use to pick quant modes per-route or per-campaign while accounting for latency, tail behavior, and mixed-precision switch overhead.

TL;DR
- Build an "iso-cost fidelity map": X-axis = per-token cost (compute + memory + switching), Y-axis = measured fidelity loss (QA accuracy delta / relative utility). Contours show equivalent end-user cost at different latency budgets.
- Compute a knee metric (knee score) from curvature of the fidelity vs cost curve for each workload; pick modes on the high marginal-fidelity per-cost side of the knee.
- Account for p99 latency inflation and mixed-precision switching as line items. Use bootstrap on eval set to get confidence bands.

Why this is different from our existing quant tooling
Most current artifacts try to optimize a single metric (e.g., average token cost or aggregate latency). This doc focuses on a multi-dimensional decision surface that explicitly encodes: (1) marginal utility per cost; (2) operational tail risk; (3) per-request mixed precision switching and cache-invalidation overhead; (4) confidence in fidelity estimates. The visual is intentionally actionable for product owners ("stay left of the green knee") and SREs (highlight p99 risk zones).

Key definitions used below
- Fidelity: relative task quality. Represent as delta_accuracy = baseline_accuracy - quant_accuracy. Lower is better (0 = no loss). For small-scale experiments we use QA/EM or task-specific accuracy. For generative tasks consider a blended metric: 0.7*QA + 0.3*KL-divergence on logit dist.
- Cost per token: sum of GPU compute cost + amortized memory + extra infra cost for mixed-precision switching. Expressed in cents/token (or normalized unit).
- Latency budget: median and p99 constraints per route.
- Knee score: second-derivative-based heuristic to identify point of rapidly diminishing returns.

Spreadsheet layout (worksheet tabs)
1) knobs_and_inputs - single-pane for knobs and global assumptions
   - model: size, baseline flops/token
   - baseline mode: FP16 (or fp32 hosted baseline)
   - hardware: GPU type, tokens/sec, price per GPU-hour
   - batch profile: median, 90th, 99th effective batch size (from A/B trace)
   - cache hit rate assumptions (prefix / KV cache)
   - switching penalty: time cost (ms) + memory copies when switching precision on the same host
   - eval set description: N samples, task, metric (QA, BLEU, perplexity)

2) perf_profiles - empirical microbenchmarks
   - rows: mode (FP16, INT8, FP8, 4b), seq_len buckets, batch sizes
   - columns: tokens/sec, p50 latency per-token-ms, p95, p99, memory-peak, flops-util
   - helpful cell: effective_tokens_per_sec_adjusted_for_cache = tokens/sec * (1 - cold_cache_fraction)

3) cost_model - computed per-mode costs
   - columns: compute_cost_per_token, mem_cost_per_token, infra_surcharge_pct, switching_cost_per_request, total_cost_per_token
   - formula notes: compute_cost = (1 / tokens_per_sec) * gpu_hour_price / 3600; mem_cost amortized by model residency and eviction rate

4) fidelity_evals - eval results and bootstrap CI
   - rows: mode, metric_mean, metric_std_err, bootstrap_2.5pct, bootstrap_97.5pct
   - include a small sample of qualitative failure modes (short bullet list) for 4b/INT8

5) iso_cost_map - the visual data grid
   - x: cost bins (0.01c/token increments or normalized units)
   - y: fidelity loss (delta accuracy)
   - each cell: expected utility = baseline_utility - loss; adjustable penalty for latency violations
   - way to compute contours: for each latency budget, restrict candidate modes to those that satisfy p99 constraint then contour equal-cost lines from total_cost and expected utility

6) knee_finder - numerical steps
   - Input: ordered (cost, fidelity_loss) pairs for a workload
   - Smooth with a small Gaussian window (sigma picked based on sample density)
   - Compute curvature k = |y''| / (1 + y'^2)^(3/2) (discrete finite difference) and normalize
   - Knee score = cost_at_max_curvature * (1 + weight*uncertainty_penalty)
   - Select mode candidates with cost <= cost_at_max_curvature * alpha (alpha defaults to 1.05) and uncertainty_penalty based on bootstrap CI width

Example scenario (toy numbers)
- Baseline FP16 QA = 78.2% on eval set (N=400)
- INT8: QA = 77.6% (delta 0.6 pts), tokens/sec = 2500, p99 per-token-ms = 0.45, compute_cost = 0.008c/token
- FP8: QA = 77.9% (delta 0.3 pts), tokens/sec = 2200, p99 = 0.38ms, compute_cost = 0.009c/token
- 4b: QA = 76.1% (delta 2.1 pts), tokens/sec = 3300, p99 = 0.60ms, compute_cost = 0.005c/token
Mixed-precision switching: 6ms cold penalty when switching to/from 4b on a host that has FP8 model already loaded (amortize if > K requests)
Knee analysis result: curvature peak near FP8 -> choose FP8 for latency-sensitive routes given an SLA of p99 <= 50ms and utility tolerance of delta <= 0.5 pts. If cost budget tight and workload tolerant, 4b is viable for background batch jobs.

Operational considerations (SRE + product)
- Tail-visibility: include p99 and p999 in the iso_cost aggregator, not just median. Knee shifts to the right when p99 cost inflation is high.
- Cold-cache switching: Prefer co-located model variants in the same process (multi-codepath) to avoid disk+warmup overhead that kills short-tail requests.
- Canary plan: deploy FP8 canary at 5% traffic for 48h with synthetic prompt set that stresses failure modes; compute bootstrap delta and update knee score.
- Billing signals: show per-route iso-cost map in Console UI with toggle for "safety margin" (how much of the left-side cost you want to preserve for future headroom).

Open questions & TODOs
- How do we standardize the blended fidelity metric across different task types? Proposal: task-specific weighting saved with the route metadata.
- Switching penalty model needs a small benchmark harness that simulates mixed-traffic with cold-starts and cross-variant locality.
- Should we include user-visible latency cost (user drop-off)? Might be approximated by converting p99-latency into expected revenue loss per-minute for revenue-generating routes.

Next steps & proposed owner
- Build the spreadsheet tabs as above (owner: Aisha) 
- Add a small benchmarking job (bench/quant-switch-over) to repo (owner: Ravi)
- UX prototyping: how to surface iso-cost contours in Console (owner: Ben)

Notes-to-self (rough)
- Keep the spreadsheet light: precompute cost-per-token rows for common GPUs (A100/H100/RTXX) and provide a small dropdown.
- Avoid overfitting knee hyperparameters; pick sensible defaults and make them editable per-workload.

References and links
- internal confluence: iso-cost-maps
- JIRA: OPT-412 for benchmarking harness
- PR: quant-playground/pull/78 (sample notebook that computes curvature and plots contour lines)

Unresolved thought: consider adding a "confidence buffer" slider in the Console that inflates perceived fidelity loss by the upper bootstrap bound when automatically recommending a mode.

End.
